title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 650bis–787 of the sequel to La Longue Marche). A 'Teichmüller system' is a discrete group 𝔊_0 with a subgroup Π_0 (geometric or surface/braid part). Its profinite completions give Π ⊂ 𝔊, and 𝔊 sits inside an arithmetic extension M, an extension of a Galois-type group by 𝔊. The data include 'inertia' maps K_i : T_0 → 𝔊_0, i ∈ I, from cyclotomic tori (loops around the divisors at infinity). On the previous page Grothendieck fixes a homomorphism (65) φ : 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(Q) into the Q-points of a pro-algebraic group scheme 𝔊_Q over Q; Π_Q is the subgroup generated by the image of Π_0. He then defines M^φ_Q as the group scheme of pairs (u, μ), with u an automorphism of 𝔊_Q and μ ∈ G_m, such that each inertia image is sent to its μ-th power up to conjugation by a local section of Π_Q: (69) u(K_i(λ)) = int(f_i)^{-1}(μλ). This is the pro-algebraic analogue of the Galois condition 'σ maps an inertia generator to a conjugate of its χ(σ)-th power'. The map χ : M^φ_Q → G_m kills the image of 𝔊_Q under inner automorphisms and so factors through Γ^φ_Q = M^φ_Q / Im 𝔊_Q (70).

This page. Suppose (𝔊_0, Π_0) is part of a Teichmüller system (Π ⊂ 𝔊 ⊂ M, with Π_0 ⊂ Π and 𝔊_0 ⊂ 𝔊). Suppose also that φ comes from a homomorphism of such systems into adelic points, M → M(A_Q), constructed by the method of the previous section. Then there is a natural homomorphism (71) M_Q → M^φ_Q, given by the action of M_Q on 𝔊_Q together with the character χ_M. It makes two diagrams commute:
- (72), left: the ladder 𝔊_0 → M, down to 𝔊(Q) → M(A_Q), down to M^φ_Q(Q) → M^φ_Q(A_Q), where the lower left vertical map is 'int'.
- (72), right: 𝔊_Q → M_Q → M^φ_Q, with the composite equal to the canonical map 'via the inner action'.

If the centre of 𝔊_Q is trivial, the inner map 𝔊_Q → M^φ_Q is injective. Grothendieck calls this hypothesis 'crédible', especially if the centre of 𝔊_0 is trivial. Then (Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M^φ_Q) is 'the' algebraic Teichmüller system attached to a homomorphism of Lie systems (Π ⊂ 𝔊 ⊂ M; Π_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0) → (Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M^φ_Q). This is a universal extension relative to φ: M^φ_Q is the largest algebraic group of cyclotomically-twisted, inertia-preserving automorphisms, a pro-algebraic Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group attached to an algebraic (not necessarily unipotent) completion of 𝔊_0. The next page treats the case where no such homomorphism M → M^φ_Q(A_Q) is given a priori, and asks when it exists, at least on an open subgroup.

Purpose: to build Q-algebraic ('motivic' or Lie-type) models of the arithmetic Teichmüller tower. Arithmetic Galois actions on profinite fundamental groups would then factor through adelic points of a Q-group defined purely by inertia and cyclotomic conditions.
errors: Trivial centre of 𝔊_0 does not in general imply trivial centre of an algebraic completion 𝔊_Q. Grothendieck flags this himself as only 'crédible'; it is a heuristic.

For int(g), g ∈ 𝔊_Q, to lie in M^φ_Q, one needs g·K_i·g^{-1} to be Π_Q-conjugate to K_i (with μ = 1). This holds when 𝔊_Q is generated by Π_Q and elements normalising each inertia class, but it is not argued on the page.
In the final line the target system should read (Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M^φ_Q). Logically it is M^φ_Q, not 𝔊_Q, that is interpreted as 'the M_Q' associated to φ; the written subscripts appear slipped.

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms of an algebraic completion of a fundamental/Teichmüller group that send inertia to conjugates of their μ-th powers, augmented to G_m (cyclotomic character)
ideas.modern_name: pro-algebraic Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group / group of special (inertia-preserving) automorphisms; cf. Drinfeld's GT(k), Ihara's special outer automorphisms
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the profinite Teichmüller tower and its automorphism group, not this algebraic-group version

ideas.what: Comparing the arithmetic extension M with adelic points of the Q-group, M → M(A_Q), so that the Galois action factors through M^φ_Q(A_Q)
ideas.modern_name: relative/weighted completion with Galois action; motivic Galois group image in adelic points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003; relative completion of mapping class groups, 2009); Deligne

ideas.what: Universal property: with trivial centre, (Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M^φ_Q) is the universal algebraic Teichmüller system receiving the given system via φ
ideas.modern_name: universal extension / automorphism-group envelope (centre-free group embedded in its inertia-respecting automorphism group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory (centre-free G ↪ Aut G); application unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, for an arbitrary algebraic (not necessarily unipotent) completion φ : 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(Q) of a Teichmüller-system group, an algebraic group M^φ_Q over Q. It is defined by cyclotomically twisted inertia-preservation, and the arithmetic group M maps to its adelic points. This anticipates the later Hain–Matsumoto relative/weighted-completion framework and pro-unipotent GT, in a uniform 'Teichmüller system' language that was never published.
missed.quote: qui est une certaine extension universelle p.r. à l'hom. donné (65) φ : 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a functorial definition of a 'GT-type group attached to any algebraic completion' (e.g. reductive or relative completions of mapping class groups), with an explicit universal property. It also raises a criterion question for when the Galois action lifts to adelic points of it (next page, (73)). The literature does not seem to formulate this in exactly this generality.

missed.claim: Whether the centre of 𝔊_Q is trivial for natural completions (needed for 𝔊_Q to embed in M^φ_Q) is left as a 'credible' hypothesis.
missed.quote: Si le centre de 𝔊_Q est trivial (ce qui est une hyp. "crédible" surtout si le centre de 𝔊_0 l'est...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Centre-freeness of relative completions of mapping class / braid-type groups is a concrete testable question.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an unpublished algebraic/adelic version of the Teichmüller–Galois formalism, foreshadowing Drinfeld's pro-unipotent GT and Hain–Matsumoto relative completions. However, the core ideas (special automorphisms, cyclotomic twist on inertia) are now well known, and the page itself is mostly formal.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the systems are written with vertical inclusions: Π ⊂ 𝔊 ⊂ M on top and Π_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0 below, with Π_0 ⊂ Π and 𝔊_0 ⊂ 𝔊.

In the left diagram (72), the long diagonal strokes are hatching or cancellation marks over the diagram, not arrows. One diagonal arrow from 𝔊(Q) to M^φ_Q(A_Q) appears drawn and partly struck through.
In the right diagram, the diagonal arrow 𝔊_Q → M^φ_Q is labelled 'can. via action int.'.
Bottom row of (72): M^φ_Q(Q) ⟷ M^φ_Q(A_Q); the double-headed arrow most plausibly stands for the inclusion induced by Q ⊂ A_Q.
